questions.q: Which statement about a chemical reaction at equilibrium is correct?
options: Forward and backward rates are equal and the concentrations are constant
The product concentration equals the reactant concentration
questions.explain: Equilibrium is dynamic — both reactions go on but, the rates being equal, the concentrations do not change. The concentrations need not be equal.

questions.q: What is the expression for K_{c} of H₂(g) + I₂(g) ⇌ 2HI(g)?
questions.explain: Products on top, reactants below, each raised to its coefficient — HI is squared.

questions.q: If K_{c} of N₂ + 3H₂ ⇌ 2NH₃ is K, what is K_{c} of 2NH₃ ⇌ N₂ + 3H₂?
questions.explain: The equilibrium constant of the reverse reaction is the inverse, 1/K.

questions.q: If K_{c} of N₂ + 3H₂ ⇌ 2NH₃ is K, what is K_{c} of ½N₂ + 3/2 H₂ ⇌ NH₃?
questions.explain: Multiplying the equation by n gives Kⁿ; for n = ½ it is K^{1/2} = √K.

questions.q: For N₂ + O₂ ⇌ 2NO at 800 K, [N₂] = 3.0 × 10⁻³ M, [O₂] = 4.2 × 10⁻³ M and [NO] = 2.8 × 10⁻³ M at equilibrium. What is K_{c}?
In K_{p} = K_{c}(RT)^{Δn}, what is Δn for N₂ + 3H₂ ⇌ 2NH₃?
questions.explain: Δn = moles of gaseous products − moles of gaseous reactants = 2 − 4 = −2.

questions.q: What is K_{p} for CaCO₃(s) ⇌ CaO(s) + CO₂(g)?
questions.explain: Pure solids do not appear in K; only the gas CO₂ does — K_{p} = p_{CO₂}.

questions.q: K_{c} of N₂ + O₂ ⇌ 2NO is 4.8 × 10⁻³¹ at 298 K. What does it mean?
options: Reactants dominate at equilibrium — the reaction hardly occurs
The reaction goes almost to completion
questions.explain: For K < 10⁻³ the equilibrium mixture is mostly reactants. K tells the extent, not the speed.

questions.q: H₂ + I₂ ⇌ 2HI, K_{c} = 57.0 (700 K). With [H₂] = 0.10, [I₂] = 0.20, [HI] = 0.40 M, Q_{c} = 8.0. Which way does the reaction go?
questions.explain: When Q < K the reaction moves towards more products, i.e. forward.

questions.q: CO + H₂O ⇌ CO₂ + H₂ (K_{c} = 4.24, 800 K). Starting with 0.10 M each of CO and H₂O, what is [CO₂] at equilibrium?
What happens to N₂ + 3H₂ ⇌ 2NH₃ when the pressure is raised at constant temperature?
questions.explain: Moles fall from 4 to 2; higher pressure favours fewer moles (forward). K does not change since T is the same.

questions.q: What happens to K of an exothermic reaction when the temperature is raised?
questions.explain: For an exothermic reaction a higher temperature shifts the equilibrium backward, so K decreases (as in NH₃ synthesis).

questions.q: What does a catalyst do to an equilibrium?
options: Helps reach equilibrium sooner without changing K
questions.explain: A catalyst speeds up both directions equally; the position of equilibrium and K are unchanged.

questions.q: What is the conjugate base of HCO₃⁻?
questions.explain: Losing a proton, the acid HCO₃⁻ gives CO₃²⁻. H₂CO₃ is its conjugate acid.

questions.q: Which of the following is a Lewis acid?
questions.explain: BF₃ is electron-deficient and accepts an electron pair. The others donate electron pairs (bases).

questions.q: About what is the pH of 1.0 × 10⁻⁸ M HCl?
questions.explain: The ionisation of water must be included: [H⁺] = 1.05 × 10⁻⁷ M, pH = 6.98. An acid cannot have pH above 7.

questions.q: What is the degree of ionisation α of 0.02 M HF (K_{a} = 3.2 × 10⁻⁴)?
questions.explain: Solving the quadratic K_{a} = cα²/(1 − α) gives α = 0.12; the pH is 2.62.

questions.q: K_{b} of NH₃ is 1.77 × 10⁻⁵. What is K_{a} of NH₄⁺? (K_{w} = 10⁻¹⁴)
What is an aqueous solution of CH₃COONa like?
questions.explain: CH₃COO⁻ + H₂O ⇌ CH₃COOH + OH⁻ — the anion of a weak acid hydrolyses and gives OH⁻, so the solution is basic.

questions.q: In a buffer [CH₃COONa] / [CH₃COOH] = 10 and pK_{a} = 4.76. What is the pH?
K_{sp} of AgCl is 1.8 × 10⁻¹⁰ at 298 K. What is its solubility S in water?
Why is AgCl less soluble in NaCl solution than in pure water?
options: The common ion Cl⁻ shifts the equilibrium towards solid AgCl
NaCl reacts with Ag⁺ and coats it
questions.explain: When Q = [Ag⁺][Cl⁻] exceeds K_{sp}, the salt precipitates, so the solubility falls. K_{sp} itself does not change (same temperature).
